The independently downloaded response matches the frozen source revision 2 SHA-256. The opening paragraph in Chapter 1 is uniquely anchored at jls-1-100. It explicitly calls Java a programming language and describes characteristics of that language. The complete citing HTML paragraph occupies zero-based half-open byte range [3954,4726) of the preserved publisher response and has SHA-256 df1273e73d0612b667353669bfb9abb5fd59fede81584fd9c8d7b6e655855b3e. The exact passage is admissible as official documentation for Oracle’s descriptive identification of Java in the Java SE 21 edition. The SCES validator accepted the category, descriptive modality, official-documentation role and scoped support edge under the Language Index adoption and rejected a governing-specification role for the same documented claim. challenge.method: Compare the exact opening paragraph with jls-1-130, the example at jls-1.2-110 and §1.4. Test whether the primary referent could be the JVM, a JDK distribution or the Java SE Platform API. Check whether the normative-looking HTML class affects the exact descriptive proposition. Apply both actual validators to the frozen claim and the Java entity projection, including the candidate source role and the governing-specification alternative.
challenge.results: The opening paragraph expressly names the Java programming language. The later opening paragraph identifies the separately specified JVM bytecode and binary format as compilation targets. Section 1.2 presents Oracle JDK as an installed tool environment for compiling and running an example. Section 1.4 distinguishes the language’s treatment of certain API classes from full platform API documentation. These passages identify distinct referents and supply no counterexample to the scoped language identity. The proposition makes an affirmative descriptive identification, and the actual admissibility check rejects treating this source binding as governing-specification support. The exact language projection passed the local validator.

limitations: The identity is scoped to Oracle’s identification of the language in the Java SE 21 specification. The registered description supplies no finding about implementation conformance, JVM behavior, JDK tooling versions, platform API coverage or identity in other editions.
The active state describes the Language Index entity record. The publisher’s introduction supplies the name and language kind.
